result.title: Improving Signals, Declining Encoder: A Known-Answer Test of Label-Free Monitoring in Self-Supervised Learning
result.comment: 17 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/nilotpal09/improving-signals-declining-encoder. Checkpoints: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23666713
result.summary: Self-supervised training is monitored without labels, through the loss and statistics of the learned features. We report a case where we know the encoders lost part of what they had learned, so we can check whether these signals noticed. We trained LeJEPA encoders on synthetic images with known generating factors. In nine of ten seeds, the readability of those factors fell abruptly and stayed down, nearly always along the same direction in factor space. Meanwhile the loss kept falling, and most of the eleven label-free signals we tracked kept improving and rated the declining runs better than runs that did not decline. Standard change-point detection rarely flagged the decline near its onset, and selecting checkpoints by these signals mostly chose ones after it.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在已知生成因子的合成图像上训练 LeJEPA 编码器，构造「已知答案」测试，检验 loss 与 11 种无标签特征统计信号能否察觉编码器对因子可读性的骤降；结果多数信号反而持续改善，变点检测也难以及时报警。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「已知答案」诊断范式可供核查 LVR 中 latent 相似度、特征统计等代理监控量是否真能反映视觉内容保留，也与信息坍缩和检查点选择的风险相关。
